Full manuscript in two months.
That was the goal.
I was on vacation in Mexico, no less, when I checked my email and saw the opportunity.
It was mid-June and the conference was happening near the city of Oaxaca.
The invitation was from a publisher looking for innovative short stories, exactly what I wanted to work on while relaxing on the beach and enjoying the sun.
I felt my ego swelling as I imagined myself being among the top contenders, sharing my story with literary experts and fellow writers.
But something unexpected happened.
My ego, which had been inflating like a hot-air balloon, began to sabotage my efforts.
Each night, instead of immersing myself in the creative process, I found myself justifying why this task was too overwhelming or why it wouldn't be good enough.
The beach breeze and the serene setting that should have inspired me only served as a stark contrast to the chaos brewing inside my mind.
I started to doubt every sentence and thought.
My initial excitement transformed into anxiety and self-doubt.
I began comparing my writing to other works I encountered in the vast expanse of literature, each comparison making my ego shrink like a deflated balloon.
What was once an exciting challenge now felt like an impossible task, one that I was sure I could not achieve without some kind of superpower.
I remember the first few days when I forced myself to sit at my small desk in the hotel room, determined to make progress.
Each time I opened my laptop, I found myself stuck, unable to move past the opening sentences.
My ego told me I was talented, but it also told me that talent wasn't enough.
It insisted that my voice was weak, my plot cliché, and my characters insipid.
These narratives began to consume me, turning my vacation into a nightmare of self-doubt.
Midway through, I realized I needed to do something drastic.
How Prepared Are You for the Revolution?
Once upon a time, not that long ago in the restaurant, food and hospitality industry, the formula for success was pretty simple to grasp.
Following the formula was widely accepted as the guaranteed path to making money.
It involved a combination of high-quality food, exceptional service, an inviting ambiance, and strategic marketing.
But today, the hospitality industry is experiencing a seismic shift—a revolution that is redefining what it means to be successful.
This transformation is being driven by a confluence of factors, from technological innovations to changing consumer behavior and environmental concerns.
The hospitality industry is on the cusp of a new era, and those who can adapt will thrive, while those who do not will struggle to keep up.
As we navigate this new landscape, it is essential to understand the key elements shaking up the industry and prepare accordingly.
First and foremost, technology is transforming every aspect of hospitality.
From online booking systems and digital payment solutions to AI-driven personalized experiences, tech is making travel more convenient, efficient, and enjoyable.
For instance, chatbots and virtual assistants are streamlining customer interactions, while mobile apps are offering real-time feedback and reviews.
Hotels and restaurants must invest in these technologies to remain competitive.
Gone are the days when paper forms and manual processes were sufficient; now, automation and data analytics are essential tools for modern businesses.
Secondly, sustainability is becoming a critical concern for both consumers and industry leaders.
Consumers are increasingly seeking eco-friendly options and ethical practices, which has led to a rise in sustainable dining and accommodation choices.
From composting food waste to using locally-sourced ingredients and reducing plastic use, the emphasis on sustainability is not just a trend but a necessity.
Companies that fail to address these issues may lose customers who prioritize green values over traditional amenities.
Thirdly, the ongoing pandemic has accelerated many changes that were already in progress.
**Gather Input from Organizations and Partners Across Vermont, to Determine What These Groups Will Be in Vermont**
Aldo Das | Nov 25, 2020 · 3 min read
As the world awaits the results of COVID-19 vaccine clinical trials, Vermont stands at a critical juncture.
The past year has exposed our vulnerabilities and highlighted the need for a resilient, interconnected, and adaptive society.
To ensure that Vermont not only recovers but thrives in the post-pandemic world, it is essential to gather input from organizations and partners across the state.
By doing so, we can determine what types of groups will be essential for our future, fostering a strong foundation for economic recovery, public health, and community well-being.
### Economic Resilience through Diverse Sector Collaboration
Vermont's economy is diverse and includes sectors ranging from agriculture and tourism to technology and healthcare.
Each sector has unique strengths and challenges that must be addressed collectively.

By convening stakeholders from agriculture cooperatives, local businesses, educational institutions, and government bodies, we can identify common goals and innovative solutions to support economic recovery.
For example, agricultural groups might collaborate with tech companies to develop sustainable farming practices using data analytics and precision agriculture.
Such partnerships can create new jobs and stimulate economic growth.
### Public Health Preparedness and Response
Public health is a collective responsibility that requires collaboration among medical professionals, public health agencies, researchers, and community leaders.
Gathering input from these diverse groups will help identify gaps in our healthcare system and prepare for future pandemics or health crises.
For instance, discussions could focus on enhancing telemedicine services, expanding mental health support, and improving access to vaccines and medical supplies.
A coordinated effort can enhance public health infrastructure, ensuring that Vermont is better equipped to respond to any crisis.
### Strengthening Community Networks
Community resilience is built on strong social connections and networks.
How to Change Your Programming to Achieve the Results You Desire
If negative thoughts turn into beliefs that determine your behavior, then the opposite holds true.
Positive thoughts and beliefs can lead to positive action.
This means we can reprogram our minds to achieve anything we set our minds to.
The power to change lies within us, and it starts with two simple yet powerful techniques that anyone can practice.
Firstly, affirmations are a cornerstone in the process of mind reprogramming.
Affirmations are positive statements designed to counteract negative beliefs or thought patterns.
By consistently repeating these statements, you can begin to shift your mindset from one of self-doubt or limitation to one of confidence and potential.

For instance, if you have a persistent belief that you’re not good enough at public speaking, start each day by repeating affirmations like, “I am a compelling speaker who inspires others,” or “Every speech I give is received with enthusiasm.” It’s crucial to believe in these affirmations deeply and sincerely; otherwise, they may not hold as much power over your subconscious.
Over time, these affirmations will replace your old, limiting beliefs with new, empowering ones.
Secondly, visualization is another effective tool for reprogramming your mind.
Visualization involves creating vivid mental images of your desired outcomes.
By regularly visualizing yourself successfully achieving your goals, you not only reinforce your beliefs but also prepare your mind and body for the actions necessary to make those goals a reality.
Imagine standing on stage delivering a fantastic speech, or walking into your ideal job interview with confidence and poise.
Visualize every detail—the sights, sounds, and feelings associated with these scenarios.
The more vivid and detailed the visualization, the stronger the impact on your subconscious mind.
Research has shown that regular visualization can boost confidence and reduce anxiety, making you more likely to take the necessary steps to reach your goals.
Together, these two methods—affirmations and visualization—can be powerful tools for reprogramming your mind.
### Why Everyone Should Consider Buying a Sex Doll
There’s nothing weird about owning a sex doll.
Most of us would, if they were cheaper.
A sex doll costs about as much as a car.
I’m talking high-end models, not the inflatable ones.
Those run around a hundred dollars; these cost thousands.
Yet, despite their steep price, sex dolls offer numerous benefits that make them a worthwhile investment for many.
Firstly, let's address the elephant in the room: privacy.
Buying a sex doll can be a private and discreet solution for those who want intimacy without having to engage in physical relationships or public encounters.
With a high-end model, you get the freedom to explore various scenarios and fantasies without the risk of judgment or unwanted scrutiny.
Secondly, sex dolls provide immense customization options.
They come in lifelike designs, with intricate details that simulate real human features.
High-end models often include advanced technology such as warmth, movement, and even responsiveness, offering a more realistic and engaging experience.
This allows individuals to create intimate moments tailored to their desires, enhancing both pleasure and emotional connection.
Moreover, owning a sex doll can alleviate loneliness and enhance self-esteem.
For people struggling with social anxiety or those who are single and desire companionship, a sex doll can serve as a source of comfort and companionship.
It provides constant availability and a sense of companionship that doesn't come with the same complexities as human relationships.
Additionally, sex dolls can improve sexual health and education.
Medical professionals recommend using sex dolls as part of sex therapy to help individuals overcome issues like erectile dysfunction, performance anxiety, or trauma-related difficulties.
High-quality sex dolls can also serve as educational tools, allowing people to learn about anatomy, techniques, and consent in a safe environment.
Safety is another significant benefit.
Engaging in consensual and safe sexual activities with a sex doll eliminates the risks associated with unsafe sex practices, including STIs and pregnancy.

Learning how to love me through creative writing has proven to be a powerful tool in my life.
My thoughts become more apparent, and it leads me to feel confident on my own.
When I am my own advocate, I can better navigate the complexities of personal growth and relationships.
Writing is not just about capturing a moment or expressing a fleeting emotion; it is a means to delve into the depths of one's psyche and emerge stronger.
In Zion National Park, as I hiked through the towering red cliffs and narrow gorges, each step was not just physical but also a journey of self-discovery.
The act of putting pen to paper (or finger to keyboard) is akin to mapping out a terrain within oneself—challenging yet rewarding.
By articulating my thoughts and feelings, I uncover hidden truths and insights that guide my actions and decisions.
Being my own advocate starts with recognizing that my voice matters.
It means standing up for myself when faced with injustice or misunderstanding.
When I write, I practice this advocacy, giving myself a platform to speak truthfully and unapologetically.
This practice builds resilience and strengthens my resolve to stand firm in my beliefs and needs.
Moreover, being your own advocate is about setting boundaries.
It's about knowing what you need and saying no when necessary.
Through writing, I have learned to articulate these boundaries clearly and respectfully.
This not only protects my well-being but also fosters healthier interactions with others.
As I write about my experiences, I find a clearer understanding of where my limits lie, allowing me to communicate these effectively in my daily life.
Self-love and advocacy are deeply intertwined.
When we learn to love ourselves, we empower ourselves to be our own advocates.
This empowerment manifests in small but significant ways—from asking for help when needed to speaking up in meetings to making time for self-care.
Dear Prospect,
How do you approach the salesman that sells a particular product you find lovely?
— is it that you buy because of humour or the way he introduces the product to you when he displays part of his ethos as a salesman?
Just know, these qualities can sometimes make all the difference.
In a world saturated with choices and competition, a good salesman isn’t just someone who sells products; he’s a storyteller who weaves the promise of a better life into every pitch.
His approach can be the spark that ignites interest, turning an ordinary interaction into something memorable.
Yet, what exactly makes a great salesman in today’s market?
Firstly, humor and charisma are invaluable assets.
A well-timed joke can lighten the mood and disarm any initial skepticism, making the customer feel more at ease.
When a salesman demonstrates that he can put himself in your shoes and understand your needs, it builds trust and rapport.
This connection is the foundation on which genuine customer relationships are built.
Secondly, an authentic ethos can be even more compelling than a clever sales pitch.
When a salesman shows integrity, passion, and a deep understanding of the product, it resonates more powerfully than just the features and benefits.
People buy not only from those who offer the best deal but also from those who inspire confidence and loyalty.
An honest and knowledgeable salesman can turn a skeptical customer into a loyal advocate for their brand.
However, the modern salesman faces a challenging landscape.
Today, information is readily available online, and consumers have more tools than ever to compare products and prices.
Therefore, the role of the salesman has evolved from merely being a mouthpiece for the company to becoming a guide and advisor.
He needs to provide value beyond simply pushing a sale.
Educating customers about their options and helping them understand why a product might meet their unique needs is a critical part of the process.
Moreover, in a digital age, the human touch remains essential.
Last week’s report about the state of women leadership in Chicago tech was a powerful reminder of where our successes are and where we can continue to improve.
The data creates actionable opportunity for everyone — from individual contributors, to executives, to investors — to contribute to a more inclusive ecosystem.
While these statistics offer a crucial snapshot of progress and areas for growth, they also highlight a significant narrative: when women lead, communities thrive.
This principle is no better exemplified than in Detroit, where women entrepreneurs are driving remarkable growth and innovation.
Detroit has faced unprecedented challenges over the years, yet it continues to emerge as a resilient and vibrant city.
The resurgence of its entrepreneurial spirit is partly due to the bold leadership and vision of women who refuse to be sidelined by traditional barriers.
Here are ten women leading the charge in Detroit's entrepreneurial growth:
**LaToya Cantrell, Mayor of New Orleans (and Detroit Resident)**
While not currently in Detroit, LaToya Cantrell’s experience in urban revitalization efforts offers valuable insights that can inform Detroit’s strategies.
Her focus on inclusive economic development underscores the importance of equitable growth, which is pivotal for Detroit’s future.
**Darcie McKeown, CEO of DTE Energy**
Darcie McKeown is at the forefront of sustainable business practices, pushing her company toward a cleaner energy future.
Her leadership is crucial as Detroit strives to become a leader in clean technology and innovation.
**Gwen Ifill, Co-Founder of Detroit Media Partners**
Gwen Ifill’s work in journalism and media has been pivotal in shaping public discourse around community issues.
By using media to empower and educate, she’s fostering a culture that values transparency and accountability.
**Suzanne Sessa, Founder of Sessa Design**
Sessa Design focuses on sustainable design solutions that benefit both the environment and local economies.
1. Let the drama happen around you, not with you
It’s a bit embarrassing for me that Charice and Johann have witnessed my continuous failures in relationships.
They have listened to my rants and given me compassionate advice in the six years we've been friends, but I’ve always been too caught up in my own world of drama to really learn from them.
I’ve seen firsthand how their healthy relationship dynamics differ from mine—and it has left me reflecting on what needs to change if I want a long-term love life that brings me genuine happiness.
2. Communication is Key
One of the most critical aspects of maintaining a healthy relationship is communication.
When Charice and Johann fight, they sit down and talk it out, and it works wonders for them.
For me, communication is more like a game of telephone—messages get lost in translation or come across as accusations instead of clear communication.
In any long-term relationship, misunderstandings and conflicts are inevitable, but the key is to address them promptly and openly.
Learning how to communicate effectively without escalating arguments into dramas can turn a tense moment into an opportunity for growth and understanding.
This means being willing to listen, empathize, and find common ground rather than clinging to our own perspectives.
3. Self-Care is Not Selfish
Another lesson I’ve learned from watching Charice and Johann’s relationship is the importance of self-care.
When I’m in a relationship, it’s easy to get so wrapped up in meeting my partner’s needs that I forget about my own.
However, true intimacy starts with knowing yourself.
Taking care of your physical, emotional, and mental health isn’t just beneficial for you—it also strengthens your bond with your partner because it shows them that you value your own well-being.
Whether it’s hitting the gym, picking up a hobby, or simply setting aside time for relaxation, making time for yourself is essential.
**The Child is the Father of Man: A Call for Childhood Excellence**
This in simple words means that the traits of childhood continue in manhood.
In other words, if we want to have better men, we must first ensure that our children grow up in environments that nurture their innate potential.
If we pay no attention to the child, he grows into a worthless youth and eventually becomes an adult who contributes little, if anything, positive to society.

The phrase "The Child is the Father of Man" was coined by William Wordsworth, and it encapsulates a profound truth: the experiences and nurturing during childhood have a direct impact on the person one becomes.
Childhood is not just a period of development; it is the foundation upon which the future of society is built.
In today's world, where social, economic, and environmental challenges seem insurmountable, we must prioritize the well-being and education of our children more than ever before.
Childhood should be seen as a sacred time, a critical phase of development that shapes our values, attitudes, and behaviors.
Neglecting this stage of life can lead to lifelong consequences, both individually and collectively.
Consider the myriad ways in which children are influenced during their formative years.
From the quality of their home environment and parental guidance to access to education and healthcare, every aspect of a child’s upbringing contributes to who they become as adults.
If we fail to provide them with the tools and support they need, we rob them of the opportunity to fulfill their potential and thrive.
Moreover, the current state of many societies often reflects the neglect or abuse some children experience.
Youth gangs, crime, and substance abuse are all too often the result of a lack of care, attention, and guidance during childhood.
By investing in the development of our children, we invest in the betterment of our communities and the world at large.
Education is a key component in shaping the minds and hearts of our youth.
